question.problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in radians, the exact solutions to the equation $cos\,(x+\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{1}{2},$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ are

${x}_{1}=$ 
{{field-1}}, $\,{x}_{2}=$ 
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{3}+n\cdot 2\pi , & \, & \, & x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{5\pi }{3}+n\cdot 2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our two equations for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\cdot 2\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{5\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\cdot 2\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\cdot 2\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+n\cdot 2\pi \end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $x=\frac{3\pi }{2}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

So, the solutions to the equation, in ascending order, are 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{6},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{3\pi }{2}.
$$
